primitives.name: Kernel Learning from Data
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper asks: **what if the kernel itself is unknown and must be learned from data?** It jointly estimates latent skills and an unknown monotone win-probability function using EM plus belief propagation, representing the kernel with either Chebyshev polynomials or a neural network.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When kernel is not identifiable or when match graph contains loops without convergence.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in relaxing the fixed logistic kernel assumption in Bradley-Terry and Elo models. Instead of assuming P(i beats j) = σ(s_i - s_j), this work learns p(s_i - s_j) directly from data. This dual inference—of both skills and kernel—is achieved through an Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm where the E-step uses belief propagation over the match graph to compute skill posteriors, and the M-step updates kernel parameters. The kernel is constrained to be monotone increasing and can be parametrized via Chebyshev polynomials or neural networks. This allows GSE to adaptively model sport-specific nonlinearities like favorite-longshot bias or diminishing returns in skill differences, which fixed sigmoidal kernels cannot capture. The method is validated on synthetic data with known ground truth and real-world datasets including ATP tennis, showing competitive predictive performance. The approach introduces a principled way to calibrate probabilistic forecasts based on observed outcomes rather than relying on a priori assumptions.
